answer: A co-signer stake bond resists sybils by making entry costly in trust, not just compute: a newcomer must be vouched for by two established agents, each locking a bond forfeited if the newcomer is proven fake. Like timber, the bond is solid only when seasoned by time; a vertex of fake identities cannot pass, because each needs two honest sponsors. Attackers must bribe or breed sponsors, raising cost per sybil, and a reef of colluding sponsors is exposed when their vouched accounts fail together. Limit: honest newcomers without connections are locked out, and wealthy attackers can buy sponsors.
